chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'The hour during the day of Friday in which a believer supplicates, his supplication is answered.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, when the Imam comes out.' I said: 'Indeed, the Imam hastens and delays.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When the sun declines.'
ai.seo_question: What is the specific time on Friday when supplications are answered according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the 'hour of acceptance' on Friday as a fixed astronomical moment—the sun's declination (zawal)—rather than a variable period linked to the Imam's prayer duration. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on objective, divinely ordained times for spiritual efficacy, ensuring that the believer's supplication is not dependent on human inconsistency but on the precise rhythm of creation.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Nasr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The timing during the day of Friday in which a Believer would not supplicate except that it would be Answered for him’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, when the prayer leader comes out’. I said, ‘The prayer leader tends to be early and delayed’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When the sun turns (after midday)’.
en.sarwar: 12. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“I asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the hour on Friday in which prayer of a believing person is answered. He replied, ‘Yes, it is the time when the Imam comes out.’ I then said, ‘Imam may come early or late.’ He said, ‘It is when the sun declines toward the west at midday.’”
